scope: Read-only source integrity, c10 shared geometry comparison, and c09 repaired candidate interior sampling

findings: Both views nominally contain the same central tree planter, pale right railing, northwest circular paving and clipped neighboring trees.
The day planter is a rounded thick ochre masonry rim; the spring planter is a narrower carved red frame with three gold capped uprights. This is a structural change, not a surface color change.
Day pale post caps are cubical, spring caps are spherical. Post/base edges and the surrounding bottom plinth differ in shape and exact position.
Tree crown silhouette, branch/trunk split, root flare, foliage masses and shadows are different.
Northwest ring curves and multiple stone-joint coordinates diverge substantially. The spring reference also retains a visible pasted west guide strip.
Historical navigation uses a third artwork basis. Neither visual resemblance nor the common macro crop establishes common navigable occupancy.
c10.decision: Pause spring row03/row04 native generation from its independently generated regional geometry. Use corresponding day native patches as exact same-frame geometry when they become available, then restrict spring edits to existing surfaces.

c09.sampleCoverage: Center 640-square of each of the sixteen 1024-square patch cores. Existing seam review and outer-boundary review remain separate.
findings: No new concrete interior geometry break, floating object, duplicated structure, stray mark, petal scatter, text or unexplained crack found in the sixteen samples.

Ring slabs have coherent bevels/grooves and consistent warm directional lighting. Stone textures remain angular hand-painted patches; no additional localized corrective edit is justified from these samples.
The lower-right foliage, trunk, small bushes, existing red/gold railing and cast shadow remain visually coherent in the sampled interiors.
